### <span class="imp imp-high" title="Importance 7.5/10" aria-label="Importance 7.5 of 10">7.5</span> NASA's Voyager 1 Reaches Historic Distance Milestone: 24-Hour Signal Delay
Voyager 1 has traveled 16.1 billion miles from Earth, becoming the first spacecraft with 24-hour signal round-trip delay, nearly 50 years after launch.

<ul class="takeaways">
<li>Voyager 1 launched in 1977</li>
<li>Crossed one-light-day distance from Earth</li>
<li>Continues interstellar journey as of November 19, 2026</li>
</ul>

### <span class="imp imp-high" title="Importance 7.5/10" aria-label="Importance 7.5 of 10">7.5</span> California Teenager's AI Model Discovers 1.5 Million Flickering Objects in NASA Sky Archive
California high school student Matteo Paz developed an AI system using NASA NEOWISE telescope data that identified 1.5 million variable astronomical objects, including rare transients and cataclysmic variables. The catalog was published in The Astronomical Journal in late 2025.

<ul class="takeaways">
<li>Student: Matteo Paz, Pasadena High School</li>
<li>AI identified 1.5 million flickering objects in NEOWISE archive</li>
<li>Analyzed nearly 200 billion rows of infrared measurements</li>
<li>Detected quasars, binary stars, supernovae, and rare transients</li>
<li>Peer-reviewed publication in The Astronomical Journal, late 2025</li>
</ul>

### <span class="imp imp-high" title="Importance 7/10" aria-label="Importance 7 of 10">7</span> NASA Conducts Successful 200-Second Test Fire of Artemis Moon Rocket Engine
NASA successfully tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 for 200 seconds on November 18, 2026 at Stenlis Space Center. The developmental engine delivered performance data to improve reliability for Artemis missions, which target lunar landing in 2028.

<ul class="takeaways">
<li>Test date: November 18, 2026</li>
<li>Engine ran full 200-second duration at Stenlis Space Center, Mississippi</li>
<li>Each SLS rocket uses four RS-25 engines generating 2 million pounds total thrust</li>
<li>Supports Artemis IV mission targeted for 2028</li>
</ul>

Sources: [ScienceDaily](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261120075551.htm) <span class="src-badge src-research">AI Web Searched</span>

### <span class="imp imp-high" title="Importance 7/10" aria-label="Importance 7 of 10">7</span> NASA Unveils PROMISE: Nuclear-Powered Rover Designed for Lunar Missions
NASA unveiled PROMISE, a nuclear-powered SUV-sized rover designed for the Moon's South Pole. Powered by plutonium-238, the rover will operate in permanently shadowed craters and drill for water ice during 14-day lunar nights. Launch targeted for late 2028 aboard Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander.

<ul class="takeaways">
<li>Rover name: PROMISE (Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration)</li>
<li>Size: 9.5 feet long, 2,260 pounds</li>
<li>Power source: plutonium-238 radioisotope thermoelectric generator</li>
<li>Can drill 1 meter deep for water ice</li>
<li>Targeted landing: late 2028 on Blue Moon Mark 1 lander</li>
</ul>
